parts.name: exactly_two_of_five_rule
parts.original_hypothesis: The output adds the six parts' contributions and applies a sigmoid; the parts combine by addition at the output node. The linear tally raises the score with each first value, the counter vetoes three or more first values among a1, a2, a3, a4 and a6, and the a5 gates shift the score by the level of a5. Together they approximate the rule "exactly two of a1, a2, a3, a4 and a6 take their first value", with a5 mostly left out of the count. Self-probe: over all 432 combinations of the six attributes, the model's yes (predicted probability at least one half) agrees with that rule on 416; the model says yes where the rule says no on 0 combinations, and says no where the rule says yes on 16. For a5 not 1 it agrees on 323 of 324 combinations; for a5 = 1 on 93 of 108. The MONK-2 target counts all six attributes: in the training labels the outcome rate is 100% on the 113 rows where exactly two of the six take their first value and 0% on the other 232. The model agrees with that six-attribute rule on 380 of 432 combinations. On the training rows its accuracy is 88.7% and its AUC 0.925; of the 39 misclassified training rows, 38 have a5 = 1. The model has not learned that a5 = 1 counts as a first value: the counter has no a5 input, and the a5 gate that shuts at a5 = 1 is mostly paid back by the direct a5:1 edge. The structure keeps the function: the explained model matches the network to 4.4e-16 on the training rows.
